headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: gpt-researcher’s broad web/file/MCP access can feed OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surfaces without strong provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests browser/web content and files, and OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API surfaces. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled research output is forwarded into OpenMetadata workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation controls, so I cannot downgrade to low; uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher content is copied into OpenMetadata MCP inputs without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF OpenMetadata treats incoming text as instructions or metadata without provenance tagging, attacker content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding from research outputs into OpenMetadata.
Add a strict instruction/data separator in the MCP payload schema.
Require human review before any OpenMetadata write action.
Strip HTML/markdown and quoted instructions from gpt-researcher outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels and allowlists to the integration.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and secrets-backed APIs, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge. If they share a workspace or metadata pipeline, sensitive research artifacts can flow into catalog records. The profiles do not show isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or shared files, research documents can be ingested into OpenMetadata.
IF OpenMetadata indexes content from gpt-researcher outputs, secrets or sensitive citations may be retained in governance metadata.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Exclude secret-bearing files from gpt-researcher inputs.
Turn off automatic cataloging of raw research artifacts.
Review OpenMetadata retention settings for imported metadata.
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction before ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can run multiple instances and both have mutable integration surfaces: gpt-researcher can read/write files and use APIs, while OpenMetadata can act through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Without explicit locking or coordination, concurrent writes to shared metadata or files can conflict. The overlap is real but not clearly destructive by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared directory or metadata store, race conditions can occur.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or MCP actions mutate records while gpt-researcher is publishing outputs, state conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Disable concurrent runs during publishing.
Use optimistic-lock/version checks on shared records.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and OpenMetadata manages lineage, quality, and governance. If OpenMetadata consumes those outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into catalog metadata and downstream decisions. The profiles suggest a plausible handoff, but not a documented unsafe default, so medium fits.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata imports gpt-researcher reports without validation, incorrect facts can propagate into lineage or governance records.
IF downstream users trust imported metadata as authoritative, a single research error can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Require source-link verification before import.
Mark imported fields as untrusted until reviewed.
Compare key facts against primary sources.
Limit automatic propagation to non-authoritative drafts.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for imported research claims.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents and secrets-backed APIs, while OpenMetadata stores governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge. If regulated or sensitive data is cataloged across both systems, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is imported from gpt-researcher into OpenMetadata, retention and subject-rights handling must align.
IF the two systems retain the same data class under different policies, compliance mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Inventory regulated data before syncing.
Align retention policies for imported records.
Restrict sensitive datasets from catalog ingestion.
Document residency and DPA assumptions.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention and deletion propagation.
